title: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death
hook: Bhima kills an elephant, and then he shouts its name across the field
tomorrow: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death

segments.voice: Last night Karna spent his one dart on Ghatotkacha, and Krishna rejoiced that Arjuna was safe. Your line: has given his life. Today, the last part of that line. Day eight hundred thirty-six.

There's an elephant on the Kaurava side named Ashvatthama. Same name as Drona's beloved son. Bhima finds the elephant, kills it with his mace, and then turns toward Drona and shouts, loud enough for the whole field: Ashvatthama is dead. It's a trick, and it was planned. Drona has been cutting through the Pandava army, and Krishna has told them, in Ganguli's telling, that the teacher can't be beaten while he holds his weapons. But if he hears that his son is dead, he'll put them down. Today, how a truthful man's half-truth ends his teacher's life.
screen: `AN ELEPHANT NAMED ASHVATTHAMA.` → `BHIMA SHOUTS THE NAME.` → `A PLANNED TRICK.`

segments.voice: Drona hears Bhima, and he doesn't believe it. Not from Bhima. There's one man whose word he trusts: Yudhishthira, known for never telling a lie. So Drona asks him directly. Is my son dead? Arjuna won't have any part of the plan. Krishna presses Yudhishthira: there are times, he argues, when a falsehood saves lives. Yudhishthira is afraid of lying, the text says, and he wants victory. So he answers: Ashvatthama is dead. And under his breath, so Drona can't hear, he adds: the elephant. Then the epic adds a detail. Yudhishthira's chariot, the text says, had always moved a little above the earth. After those words, it sinks and runs along the ground like everyone else's. Drona, his heart broken, lays down his weapons. He sits on his chariot and turns inward, in yoga. Dhrishtadyumna, the prince of Panchala, rushes at him with a sword. Arjuna cries out to take him alive. Too late. Dhrishtadyumna strikes, and the teacher of both houses is dead. Here's what the epic won't let go of. The trick worked. The war turned. And the man known for his truth paid for it with the thing he was known for, and the ground itself took note. Drona's command ends here, and Karna will lead next.
screen: `"IS MY SON DEAD?"` · `"...THE ELEPHANT"` · `THE CHARIOT TOUCHES GROUND` · then, large: `DRONA LAYS DOWN HIS WEAPONS`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your breath settle. Think of a time you told a half-truth, the true words with the important part said quietly or not at all. No need to punish yourself. Breathe in, and remember what you said. Breathe out, and feel how it sat with you afterward, light or heavy. Just notice the weight. If you pray, you can bring that moment into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Drona. The teacher of both houses, who laid down his weapons when the one man he trusted said his son was dead.
Your line: the ground itself took note. Today, say the whole truth once where a half-truth would be easier. Tomorrow, Karna: the wheel stuck, the death. Day eight hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: Yudhishthira's half-truth about Ashvatthama is told in the Drona Parva, and Hindu storytellers and teachers return to it when they talk about truthfulness, dharma and the costs of the war.

pairs: said the elephant under his breath
refused the plan, cried take him alive

myth: an elephant with the same name was killed; his son was alive.
Yudhishthira's chariot sank to the ground after his words
the text says it had moved above the earth until then.
Drona died fighting with his bow in hand
he laid down his weapons and sat in yoga before Dhrishtadyumna struck.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. your teacher asks you, the man who never lies, whether his son is dead. what do you say?
options: tell him plainly that his son is alive.
say Ashvatthama is dead, and whisper the elephant.
fork.reveal: Yudhishthira says Ashvatthama is dead and adds the elephant under his breath. His chariot sinks to the ground.

original.note: Drona's son, and the name of the elephant Bhima killed.

trapdoor: what you thought: Yudhishthira told a lie.
what it means: he told a half-truth, the true words with the key part said too quietly to hear.
what a scholar hears: the chariot touching the ground marks the cost: even a half-truth changes the truthful man's place in the world.
recall: bites Nala and changes his shape
waits for a lapse, then enters Nala

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Drona-vadha Parva), the elephant Ashvatthama, Yudhishthira's words and Drona's death

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Krishna advises the plan, Arjuna disapproves, and Krishna's argument about falsehood saving life.
Confirm the chariot detail: Ganguli gives a height above the ground (left out here) and says it touches the earth after the words.
Confirm Drona sits in yoga after laying down his weapons, Arjuna's cry to take him alive, and Dhrishtadyumna's sword.
Editor: cut the superlatives 'only one man on the field' and 'proudest of'.
'Known for never telling a lie' reflects Yudhishthira's reputation in the text; a Keeper may prefer 'known for his truthfulness'.
Original word अश्वत्थामा: confirm form and pronunciation.
Auditor: no change; facts checked against Drona-vadha Parva (Arjuna dissents, Krishna argues, half-spoken "elephant", chariot touches ground, sword of Dhrishtadyumna).
